svg.title: How a visitor reaches the site and where their answer comes from
svg.desc: A top-to-bottom map of one visit. Someone looking for Medicare help opens the site in a browser. The request arrives at CloudFront, which is the only way in: the instance security group admits CloudFront's managed prefix list and nothing else, so the public address cannot be dialled directly. CloudFront forwards to Caddy on the single instance, which terminates origin TLS using a certificate it renews over DNS-01, and proxies inward to the Next.js application container. The application reads content from Payload's tables and writes lead, Scope of Appointment and do-not-contact records to the same Postgres container, whose data directory is a bind mount on a separate EBS volume that outlives the instance. Images are served from an S3 bucket. Three outbound dependencies sit to the side: Cloudflare Turnstile verifies that a form submitter is human, SES sends the acknowledgement and the agency notification, and the MedicarePRO CRM receives leads. The CRM is never called during the visitor's request; a host timer posts to a local job route once a minute and that is what delivers. Every secret the application needs is rendered from SSM Parameter Store into a file on the box at boot, and none of it is reachable from the browser.
